title: secure_transport RH3 validation diverges from aligned survey (blackholes HBH+RH3 downward traffic)
description: Security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-xyix: rust/lichen-node/src/secure.rs secure_transport (secure.rs:1932-1950) rejects any RH3 not in first position, requires routing_len >= 24, and requires octets 6-7 plus the pad low nibble to be zero. The aligned survey (rpl_stack/util.rs) and the C router admit HBH-then-RH3, the 8-octet degenerate RH3, and ignored reserved bits (pinned by srh_admission.json vectors hop_by_hop_then_routing_in_transit, degenerate_zero_address_consumed, reserved_ignored_octets_admitted). receive.rs:244 runs secure_datagram_from_received before the survey on every non-RPL datagram, so RPL relays drop legitimately shaped downward traffic where C forwards it (availability divergence, and a survey-vs-gate contradiction within one binary). Fix: align secure_transport's RH3 parsing/validation with survey_routing_headers policy.
close_reason: Fixed (commit f37d392e10 on fix-secure-rh3-nuz5 branch, heft worktree, origin/main lineage). secure_transport's RH3 admission aligned with survey_routing_headers policy (C-parity, srh_admission.json): (1) HBH-then-RH3 chains admitted (bounded: HBH unique, first position, ext bounds enforced); (2) the degenerate 8-octet RH3 (zero addresses, SL=0) admitted — payload follows; (3) reserved octets beyond the Cmpr/Pad bits ignored — Cmpr octet and Pad high nibble still enforced (survey parity); (4) SL<hop_limit, SL<=address_count, and repeated/nested extension rejection kept; (5) the in-transit SL>0 final-destination formula preserved verbatim (pre-existing, and unreachable-at-consumption since relays forward via the survey). This un-blackholes HBH+RH3 downward traffic that the survey and C router admit. New unit test secure_transport_admits_hbh_then_rh3_degenerate_and_ignored_reserved pins all five behaviors. VALIDATED: full lichen-node lib suite 321 passed — the only 2 failures are rpl_stack::multicast_dio_and_dis + three_rpl_stacks (worker-6's 0l4q stale-timing migration on origin/main, pre-existing, unrelated: they assert the old immediate unicast DIO timing). Reviews: passes 1+2 on kimi-k3 PASS (relaxation is not a weakening: Cmpr/Pad enforcement kept, OSCORE gate hard-gated to UDP, repeated extensions rejected); pass 3 delegated twice with timeouts — completed by self per fallback protocol (bounds arithmetic shown above). Full-suite rerun recommended after 0l4q lands.
